descriptions.text: The BorrowerOperationsV6 contract's sell() function accepts caller-supplied parameters including sellingCode (arbitrary calldata), tokenHolder, inchRouter, integratorFeeAddress, and whitelistedDex and then performs an external call using that calldata without validating the target/selector or enforcing access control. The attacker pointed whitelistedDex (and tokenHolder/integrator) at their own contract and crafted sellingCode as privilegedLoan(WBNB, 20 ether), causing the privileged contract to execute the attacker-controlled call path and release 20 WBNB. Because sell() does not restrict who can call it or constrain the encoded action, it became an arbitrary-call primitive operating with the protocol's privileges. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0xc291d70f281dbb6976820fbc4dbb3cfcf56be7bf360f2e823f339af4161f64c6 Analysis: https://bscscan.com/address/0x8c7f34436C0037742AeCf047e06fD4B27Ad01117#code

TokenHolder was exploited on BNB Chain on 2025-10-08 in a transaction that moved 20 WBNB through a contract flow associated with a public BorrowerOperationsV6.sell() reproduction. Public exploit reproductions suggest the issue involved attacker-controlled calldata and insufficient validation of externally supplied execution parameters, but the deployed victim implementation and exact vulnerable call path were not independently verified. The exact deployed vulnerability could not be independently verified from the available evidence.
